summary: Meta's Muse Code terminal coding agent, powered by Muse Spark 1.2.
$comment: Muse Code shipped 2026-08-05 as a macOS/Linux beta (Meta Superintelligence Labs). Everything declared below comes from Meta's launch materials: the binary is `muse`, `muse --version` confirms an install, `muse exec "<prompt>"` is a headless one-shot, the default model is muse-spark-1.2, and /plan, /grill and /goal ship as built-in skills. Four blocks are deliberately NOT declared because no public reference documents them and no Muse install was reachable from this machine to probe: modelSelection (the model flag's spelling is unknown), mcpConfig (path and format unknown), skillIntegration (Muse has native slash commands, but the directory a user skill installs into is undocumented), and a resume argv (the runtime keeps a replay-exact local event log and restarts after a crash, but no `--resume`/`--session-id` flag is documented). Each is a config-only flip — run `muse --help` against a real install and fill the block in; no code change is needed, because bundled plugins are directory-scanned and AgentCli is an open string. A FIFTH block is deliberately absent and load-bearing: agentStateSpec. Hooks are the only supported status mechanism (decision of record 2026-08-31), and Muse's beta cannot deliver them — its docs describe a .muse/hooks.json registration and a `muse hooks` CLI, but beta 0.2.1 silently ignores both; hooks only function through an experimental plugin path (MUSE_EXPERIMENTAL_PLUGINS=1) that promises breaking changes before GA. Without the spec, Muse is install/detect-only: it is hidden from agent pickers, refused by agent.launch, and reported agentSelectable: false by cli.runtime.list. When Muse's hooks GA, author the agentStateSpec here (its hook contract reportedly matches Claude Code's exactly, so the settings-json or owned-json kind should fit) and every surface re-admits it with zero code changes.

manual.$comment: Only `manual` is declared. Muse's approval-bypass flag (if it has one) is undocumented, and resolvePermissionPreset in src/main/plugin-render.ts degrades an undeclared auto/bypass DOWN this ladder to `manual` rather than passing an unknown flag through — which that code notes is fatal to the CLI. Guessing a flag name here would be the one failure mode the ladder exists to prevent. Add the higher rungs once `muse --help` names the real flags.
manual.label: Manual — Muse prompts for approvals

promptInjection.$comment: Same reasoning as the grok manifest, and for the same reason: Muse's interactive TUI documents no positional prompt argument (`muse exec` is a one-shot, not a session), and its real input-ready marker is unknown. The pattern (?!) never matches by design — any guessable marker would match the startup banner before the TUI accepts input, swallowing the keystrokes and cancelling the timeout fallback, while a late post-timeout match would inject a second copy. Never-match makes delivery deterministic: exactly one injection, via the runtime's timeout fallback, once the TUI has had timeoutMs to become ready. If a real install confirms `muse "prompt"` works interactively, flip mode to positional-arg.

contextInjection.$comment: Muse documents no system-prompt flag and no instructions env var. Prompt fallback.

wsl.$comment: Inferred, not documented: Meta ships Muse Code for macOS and Linux only, and WSL is Linux, so the Linux installer is offered there. No win32 block exists on purpose — there is no native Windows build to install, and an entry that cannot succeed is worse than none.
wsl.label: Official installer in WSL (recommended)

capabilities.$comment: toolUse is true — Muse Code plans, edits, runs tools and coordinates background agents, which is the whole product. resumeSession is false because no resume flag is documented; its event-log restart-safety is an in-process guarantee, not a caller-driven resume, and the confirm-first discipline says an unverified resume path must not risk a lost conversation. sessionIdFromCaller is false because launch mints no session id. mcpServers is false because no MCP support is documented — false means the app never offers an attach that would silently do nothing.
